clinical_scope.population: Adults and young people aged 16 years or older unless otherwise specified by local protocol
excluded_populations: pediatric specialty pathways unless explicitly validated
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Pulmonary Embolism.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

distinctions.description: PE may cause chest pain and troponin elevation due to right ventricular strain; evaluate VTE risk, hypoxemia, imaging, and hemodynamic profile.

basic_info.working_definition: Pulmonary embolism is obstruction of the pulmonary arterial circulation, most commonly by thrombus from venous thromboembolism.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: Symptoms are nonspecific and may mimic pneumonia, ACS, anxiety, asthma/COPD, heart failure, pneumothorax, or aortic disease.
Syncope, unexplained tachycardia, hypoxemia, or pleuritic pain may be the only clues.
D-dimer can be misused if clinical probability is not considered.
Hemodynamic instability suggests high-risk PE requiring urgent imaging or bedside pathway.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: Hemodynamically unstable PE is immediately life-threatening; stable cases still require structured probability-based diagnosis.

activation_logic.minimum_activation: Dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, syncope, hemoptysis, unexplained hypoxemia/tachycardia, or DVT symptoms plus VTE risk context or objective cardiopulmonary abnormality.

weak_activation_patterns.reason: D-dimer is nonspecific without probability context.

symptom_to_candidate_retrieval.scoring_warning: Weights are for retrieval and explanation only. They are not calibrated probabilities and must not be used as a diagnostic score.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is the patient hypotensive, in shock, or hemodynamically unstable?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Use high-risk PE pathway; consider bedside echo/urgent CTPA if feasible.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Proceed with stable PE diagnostic algorithm.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Cannot determine high-risk boundary without vitals.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: What is the clinical pretest probability using a validated or local pathway?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Use probability to guide D-dimer or imaging.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If low and PERC negative in appropriate setting, PE may be unlikely.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is D-dimer indicated and interpretable for this probability group?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Negative appropriate D-dimer may help exclude PE in low/intermediate probability.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Positive D-dimer requires imaging context; it does not confirm PE.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is definitive imaging available: CTPA, V/Q scan, or DVT ultrasound when applicable?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Confirm or refute PE and define clot burden/RV strain.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If negative and high suspicion persists, reassess quality and alternatives.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Imaging missing; PE cannot be confirmed/excluded.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are RV dysfunction, biomarkers, or shock present?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Low-risk pathway if stable and no RV strain.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Could ACS, dissection, pneumonia, pneumothorax, heart failure, or asthma/COPD explain the presentation?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: PE remains favored if imaging/probability support it.

distinguishing_features: Chest pain, dyspnea, troponin elevation can overlap; ACS more often has ischemic ECG pattern and coronary risk context.
Abrupt tearing pain, pulse/BP differential, neurologic deficit, mediastinal findings.
Fever, cough, infiltrate, inflammatory markers; PE may have low-grade fever and pleuritic pain.
Sudden pleuritic pain and dyspnea with unilateral breath-sound changes.
Orthopnea, edema, pulmonary edema, elevated natriuretic peptides; may coexist with PE.
Wheezing and obstructive history; PE should be considered if sudden, hypoxemic, pleuritic, or VTE risk.

final_assessment.safety_statement: Clinical decision support only; urgent clinician assessment is required when a high-risk condition is suspected.

evidence_sources.title: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism
evidence_sources.publisher: European Society of Cardiology / European Respiratory Society
key_points: Acute pulmonary embolism symptoms are nonspecific and include dyspnea, chest pain, presyncope/syncope, and hemoptysis.
Diagnostic strategy depends on hemodynamic stability, clinical probability, D-dimer, CTPA/VQ imaging, and risk stratification.

must_not: Do not make an autonomous definitive diagnosis.
Do not use a single symptom, sign, laboratory result, score, or imaging clue as a standalone rule-in or rule-out criterion.
Do not provide patient-facing reassurance when critical red-flag data are missing.
Do not ignore competing high-risk differential diagnoses.
Do not replace local emergency, specialty, or hospital protocols.
Do not generate medication orders; recommend clinician-led pathway activation instead.
Do not diagnose PE from D-dimer alone.
Do not exclude high-probability PE with an inappropriate D-dimer strategy.
Do not overlook PE in syncope or unexplained hypoxemia.
must_do: Use this graph for candidate retrieval, missed-diagnosis risk reduction, and guideline-based verification.
Separate supporting evidence, evidence against, and missing critical information.
State whether verification is complete, partial, impossible from available data, or contradicted.
Include differential diagnoses that can mimic the condition.
Trace guideline-dependent claims to evidence IDs.
Mark output as clinical decision support requiring qualified clinician review.
Always separate hemodynamic stability from stable diagnostic probability pathway.
Always report whether imaging confirmation is available.
